clue.text: Sudden outburst from Bill Church's son

parts.note: AC is short for account, which is a bill
CE stands for Church of England, and the 's adds an S
S is the usual abbreviation for son in family trees

explanation.surface: A child of the clergyman Bill lets fly with an angry outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the possessive 's on Church supplies a letter, giving CES.
explanation.definitionFit: An access of rage or coughing is a sudden fit, an older sense of the word.

clue.text: Instrument placed on floor to get firm measurement internally

indicators.note: the measurement is placed inside the abbreviation for firm

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm
an ell is an old measure of length for cloth

explanation.surface: A musical instrument stands on the floor so its maker can measure it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition notes that the instrument rests on its spike on the floor when played.
explanation.definitionFit: The large bowed string instrument played seated with its spike on the floor.

clue.text: A gentle do, preposterously drawn out

indicators.note: preposterously means absurdly, so the letters are rearranged into nonsense order

explanation.surface: A mild party is described as absurdly long-winded.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stretched to a greater length is lengthened.

clue.text: Tunnel required for vehicle going up road

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
a way is a road, as in Fosse Way

explanation.surface: A tunnel is needed so a vehicle can climb the road.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground passage under a road or a railway under a city is a tunnel.

clue.text: Take away pamphlet written by journalist

indicators.note: the pamphlet is set down after the journalist, so the journalist's letters come first

parts.note: a sub is a sub-editor, a newspaper journalist
a tract is a short religious or political pamphlet

explanation.surface: Someone is told to remove a leaflet that a reporter wrote.
explanation.definitionFit: To deduct something is to remove it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: In a man's domain it's conventional to refuse to budge

indicators.note: the conventional phrase is placed inside the man's name

parts.note: Stan is a man's name, with the possessive giving Stan's
the done thing is what convention demands
ground is territory or domain

explanation.surface: On a man's property it is customary to resist being moved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' sends the conventional thing inside the man's name; 'domain' then follows as a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold firm and not retreat is an idiom for not yielding.

clue.text: Inferior horse that's outside railing?

parts.note: inferior means bad

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is goes around the horse

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is
a nag is a horse, usually a poor one

explanation.surface: A poor horse stands outside the fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Railing' looks like a fence, but the question mark points to railing as mocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Teasing banter is good-humoured railing, or mockery.

clue.text: Recommendation for mercy for motor-cyclist perhaps

definitions.meaning: a jury may add a note to its verdict asking for leniency
someone on a motorbike or horse

explanation.definitionFit: A rider is a clause added to a verdict, and also one who rides a motorbike, for example.

clue.text: Opportunity out east to keep a horse and coach

indicators.note: the shortened word holds the horse inside it
the east is put out, so its letter goes

parts.note: a chance is an opportunity
an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: There is a chance in the east to keep a horse and carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out east' removes the letter for east from the opportunity, and 'to keep' wraps the shortened word round the horse; 'a' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A charabanc was an early open motor coach used for outings.

clue.text: Plank a river creature used in the Deluge

indicators.note: the river and creature are placed inside the word for the Deluge

parts.note: the Deluge is Noah's Flood
R is the standard abbreviation for river on maps
a boar is a wild pig, a creature

explanation.surface: A wild beast is carried along on a river during Noah's Flood, clinging to a plank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used in' puts the river and creature together inside the flood, just before its final letter; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A board laid across joists to make a floor is a plank.

clue.text: Chapter head in "Pride and Prejudice"

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words of the novel's title

explanation.surface: The opening of a chapter of Jane Austen's novel is pointed to.
explanation.walkthrough: The run straddles the two words: pri-DE AN-d. 'Chapter head' looks like the start of a book chapter, but it is the head of a cathedral chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a cathedral's governing body of canons is its dean.

clue.text: Tall workman called for in the script

parts.note: tall means long in height
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A tall labourer is required for a part in a play script.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing by hand rather than in shorthand or type is a form of handwritten script.

clue.text: Fellow' taking degree in a medieval language

annotationWithheld.why: Fellow taking degree in a medieval language (6), scan agrees: MAN is fellow, but no reading of 'taking degree in a' yields the remaining N, O, R
annotationWithheld.clue: Fellow' taking degree in a medieval language

clue.text: Assist with President Truman's inauguration

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, a US President

indicators.note: an inauguration is a beginning, so the first letter of the name is taken

explanation.surface: Someone helps out at Harry Truman's swearing-in ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'President' looks like Truman himself; it is Abe Lincoln.
explanation.definitionFit: To aid or encourage someone, often in wrongdoing, is to help them.

clue.text: She symbolises this island, as a rule

definitions.text: She symbolises this island, as a rule

parts.words: She symbolises this island, as a rule
parts.note: the helmeted female figure on coins personifying Great Britain, with 'rule' recalling the patriotic song about her ruling the waves

explanation.surface: A woman stands as the emblem of the nation, usually.
explanation.definitionFit: The female figure with trident and shield is the emblem personifying Great Britain.

clue.text: Clumsily patching clothing for the retired

indicators.note: done clumsily, the letters of the word are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is awkwardly mending clothes meant for pensioners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The retired' are not pensioners but people who have gone to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cap worn in bed was headwear for those who had turned in for the night.

clue.text: Poorly rated philosopher's dreary routine

indicators.note: poorly signals the letters are badly arranged

parts.note: John Stuart Mill was an English philosopher

explanation.surface: A thinker who is ranked low has a dull daily grind.
explanation.definitionFit: A monotonous round of tasks is a tedious grind.

clue.text: Crapulence makes us suspend deliveries

parts.note: to hang is to suspend
in cricket, an over is a set of six deliveries by one bowler

explanation.surface: Drunken sickness forces a halt to the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes us' is a link. Cricket is a British bat-and-ball game; bowlers deliver the ball in overs of six.
explanation.definitionFit: Crapulence is sickness after drinking too much, the morning-after headache.

clue.text: Empty boast by young female weightlifter

parts.note: wind is idle talk or empty bragging
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A young woman's boast about her lifting strength is just hot air.
explanation.definitionFit: A winch turned by a crank to haul up heavy loads lifts weights.

clue.text: King leaves vessel to practise engraving

indicators.note: the king departs, so his letter is taken out of the boat's name

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing vessel
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch abandons his ship to take up engraving.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut a design into metal with acid is to engrave it.

clue.text: Posh garment worn in confinement

indicators.note: the posh letter is worn inside the garment

parts.note: a dress is a garment
U stands for upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: A smart outfit is worn by someone in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: U as upper class is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress is constraint or imprisonment, an old sense of the word.

clue.text: Short poem about a royal garment

indicators.note: the poem goes around the other letters

parts.note: a song is a short lyric poem
R stands for royal, as in RN for Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A brief verse is written about a garment worn by royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: A and R go between S and ONG. 'A royal garment' reads as one phrase, but only 'garment' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrap of cloth worn round the waist in South-East Asia is a garment.

clue.text: Magazine for key workers?

definitions.meaning: a musical instrument whose keys are worked

explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a newspaper or journal, and a keyboard instrument operated by keys.

clue.text: Game played by canons without hesitation

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the canons enclose the hesitation

parts.note: a canon in music is a round, sung in overlapping parts
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Churchmen play a game without pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canons' suggests clergy, but they are musical rounds; 'without' is the old sense of outside, so the canons enclose the hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: A bat-and-ball sport played in British schools, like baseball, is a game.

clue.text: Most of an old widow's surviving belief

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: relict is an old word for a widow

explanation.surface: An elderly widow keeps most of her old faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A survival of a custom or belief from the past is a holdover.

clue.text: Shakespearian actor given Pistol's backing?

indicators.note: backing means the word is read backwards

parts.note: pistols are guns, with the 's read as plural

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean player has the support of Pistol, another character.
explanation.walkthrough: Pistol is a Shakespeare character, but here he is just a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Snug the joiner is one of the amateur players in A Midsummer Night's Dream, an actor in the play within the play.

clue.text: University literary hack in farewell entertainment

indicators.note: the university and hack are put inside the word for farewell

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell
a devil is a hack who does work for a writer or lawyer

explanation.surface: A university's hack writer appears in a goodbye show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts the university letter and the hack inside the Latin farewell, splitting it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Variety theatre of songs, sketches and acts is a type of stage show.

clue.text: Affected fellow born in France — a revolutionary

parts.note: a fellow is a man
ne is French for born
a red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A pretentious man was born in France and became a revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Mannered behaviour is artificial or stilted, a synonym for affected.

clue.text: Only when detailed, one gives comfort

indicators.note: detailed means having its tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: sole means only
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: Only when given full details does someone find consolation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' looks like 'in detail' but means de-tailed: SOLE loses its E.
explanation.definitionFit: Consolation in distress is comfort, a plain synonym.
